pages.title: Settings > Account > Set Up Ask Elmer, Elmer Voice and Elmer Control
pages.text: ﻿ Settings > Account > Set Up Ask Elmer, Elmer Voice and Elmer Control Set Up Ask Elmer, Elmer Voice and Elmer Control << Click to Display Table of Contents >> Navigation: Settings > Account > Set Up Ask Elmer, Elmer Voice and Elmer Control Elmer adds three related capabilities to RigPi: Feature Purpose Ask Elmer Answers RigPi and amateur-radio questions using an indexed technical library, approved live station and internet data, deterministic tools, and information supplied by the operator. Sources used for an answer are identified in its References section. Elmer Voice Accepts spoken questions and commands, reads answers aloud, and can provide live transcription and translation. Elmer Control Provides a compact command drawer in the Tuner and Keyer windows for safe radio, CW, macro, scanning, and recording actions. Requirements • An internet connection. • A current RigPi release containing Elmer. • A paired RigPi Elmer Service connection. • For voice input, microphone permission and a secure HTTPS RigPi connection. A local secure browser context may also work. No OpenAI setup is required. RigPi users do not need a ChatGPT subscription, OpenAI account, or personal API key. RigPi.net supplies the hosted service through the station's Elmer plan or beta allowance. Connect the RigPi Elmer Service 1. Sign in to RigPi with an administrator account. 2. Open Settings > Accounts > User Settings . 3. Locate RigPi Elmer Service and select Configure . 4. If the station is not connected, enter a recognizable station name. 5. Provide the displayed six-character approval code to the RigPi Elmer administrator. Approval may take up to 24 hours. 6. You may leave the page and return later. RigPi checks the request again and displays Connected after approval. Select View Usage to see the station plan, allowance, questions, tokens, response timing, and voluntary feedback totals. Usage is shared by the accounts on that physical RigPi. Disconnect immediately revokes the protected station credential. Ask Elmer, hosted voice processing, and cloud command interpretation will stop until the station is paired again. Use Ask Elmer 1. Open Help > Ask Elmer . 2. Enter a question in everyday language. Press Enter to ask; use Shift+Enter for a new line. To ask by voice, tap Elmer PTT , speak after the tone, then tap it again when finished. No wake phrase is required. 3. Elmer searches the RigPi knowledge collection and, when appropriate, station-local live services such as QRZ, the onboard FCC database, repeater data, or shortwave schedules. 4. Use the speaker control to turn spoken answers on or off. The animated voice indicator shows when Elmer is listening or speaking. 5. Use Copy to copy the formatted answer. Links and approved images remain available in the displayed answer. 6. Rate the answer from 1 through 10 and optionally explain why. Submitted feedback helps improve RigPi. Example questions include: • How do I configure an IC-7300 for remote audio and CAT control? • How do I set up remote CW keying? • Start CW simulator • Show me a photograph and biography for W6HN • Show K8AJS on a map • Find all ham clubs within 40 miles of ZIP 44691 • Show all Extra-class hams within 10 miles of Wooster, Ohio • What shortwave stations are broadcasting in Spanish now? • What are the W8WOO repeater frequencies? References marked Official Help are the preferred source for current RigPi operation. Community posts and contributed files may describe older releases; Elmer identifies uncertainty and conflicting procedures when the evidence permits. Ask Elmer information sources Ask Elmer selects sources according to the question. A normal answer uses only the relevant items and identifies them in its References section. Availability of live sources depends on the signed-in RigPi account, configured external accounts, station connection, and internet access. Indexed knowledge library Source Information provided Official RigPi Help Current operating instructions and the preferred authority for RigPi features and settings. RigPi GitHub RigPi source code, README material, releases, issues, issue discussions, and other project documentation. Hamlib GitHub Hamlib source code, radio backends, documentation, releases, issues, issue discussions, and wiki material. WSJT-X The official WSJT-X 3.0 User Guide plus WSJT-X source, documentation, releases, and issue discussions. RigPi Groups.io Community support messages, discussion threads, and contributed files. These may describe older RigPi versions and are treated as community evidence. SIGIDWiki Amateur Radio Signals Community-maintained descriptions and examples of amateur-radio signal types and digital modes. 47 CFR Part 97 The current Amateur Radio Service rules imported from the official eCFR developer service. Live, local, and calculated sources Source Information provided Operator and conversation context The current question, an attached image, recent Ask Elmer exchanges, and relevant signed-in station details supplied by RigPi. RigPi station databases and live services Selected radio, station and user settings, radio status and readback, rigctld and rotctld state, CW/keyer runtime, serial-device availability, browser-audio status, and other read-only diagnostic observations. RigPi frequency intelligence BandActivity customary operating ranges and calling frequencies, BandPrivileges license and emission privileges, and the operator's configured country, IARU region, and license class. Activity entries are guidance rather than exclusive allocations or permission to transmit. RigPi local logbook Previous contacts with a requested callsign when the question calls for logbook history. QRZ XML, HamQTH XML, and the RigPi onboard FCC database Callsign identity, license and location details, grid and coordinates when available, plus QRZ biography, photographs, and station information when authorized by the configured account. NCVEC Question Pool Committee Current Technician, General, and Amateur Extra question pools, answer keys, diagrams, and syllabus topics used by Elmer's study questions and simulated exams. HearHam Cached repeater-directory records and approximate transmitter-site coordinates. ILGRadio and EiBi Cached shortwave broadcast schedules. Licensed ILGRadio data remains for local RigPi use and is not redistributed; EiBi provides fallback schedule coverage. Open-Meteo Current, forecast, and historical gridded weather plus supporting forecast data used for operating and antenna-safety questions. NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center Solar-flux, geomagnetic, and planetary K-index forecast information used in propagation guidance. DX Summit Recent cluster spots used to find observed path and time patterns. Spots are reports, not confirmed contacts or propagation guarantees. WorldFactbook.io Current country profiles for international callsign and country questions. Natural Earth and OpenStreetMap Country outlines, map tiles, place lookup, and geographic context. Callsign markers use callbook coordinates when available; inferred or approximate locations are identified. RigPi Ham Tools Deterministic antenna, wavelength, transmission-line, power, impedance, unit-conversion, and related amateur-radio calculations. The language model is the explainer, not the evidence. It organizes and explains the retrieved material. Official rules and current RigPi Help outrank community reports; live observations are timestamped or described as snapshots, and customary activity information is not presented as regulatory authorization. CW practice and contest simulators Ask Elmer includes browser-based CW receiving practice. Enter CW simulator to resume the last-used exercise, or ask for a specific exercise by name. Use the Practice selector to move between exercises without losing the selected character speed, spacing speed, or band conditions. Practice mode What it sends CW QSO Natural, varied contacts containing callsigns, signal reports, names, locations, rigs, power, antennas, and closing exchanges. Callsigns Random amateur-radio callsigns for focused copying practice. Random 5-character groups Five groups of five mixed letters and numbers. Sweepstakes Contest Serial number, precedence, callsign, check, and ARRL/RAC section. ARRL Field Day Operating class and ARRL/RAC section. Field Day does not use an RST in its exchange. DX Pileup A DX station and overlapping callers, including partial-call requests, occasional callers transmitting at the wrong time, and selectable pileup intensity. CQ WW RST and CQ zone. CQ WPX RST and a progressive serial number. ARRL International DX W/VE stations copy RST and transmitter power from DX stations; DX stations copy RST and state or province from W/VE stations. 1. Select the exercise, character speed, spacing speed, and band conditions. A spacing speed below the character speed provides Farnsworth practice. 2. With the copy box focused, press Enter to play the CW. 3. Type everything copied and press Enter to check it. 4. Press Enter again for the next callsign or exchange, then press Enter once more to play it. Clean, light, and busy conditions add progressively stronger recorded receiver noise, off-frequency QRM, and fading. DX Pileup provides separate light, moderate, and heavy caller settings. The selected exercise and settings are remembered for the signed-in callsign in that browser. Practice is safe and self-contained. The simulator generates CW audio in the browser. It does not key the radio, assert PTT, change the station, or require an SDR audio connection. Use Ham Tools Ask Elmer includes deterministic amateur-radio calculators and operating references. RigPi Ham Tools performs the numerical work and Elmer explains the result, so the answer is based on the displayed inputs and formula rather than an estimated language-model calculation. Examples include: • How long is a dipole for 14.2 MHz? • Design a quarter-wave ground-plane antenna for 146.52 MHz • Give me starting HB9CV dimensions for 144.3 MHz • Design a 10-turn axial helix for 2.4 GHz • What is the wavelength at 7.2 MHz? • Estimate the loss in 75 feet of LMR-400 at 146 MHz with 100 watts • What is the VSWR with 100 watts forward and 4 watts reflected? • Using Ohm's law, what current flows with 13.8 volts and 50 ohms? • Convert 37 dBm to watts • What is the output after 3 dB loss from 100 watts? • Spell W6HN phonetically • What does QSY mean? Use calculated antenna dimensions as starting values. Element diameter, insulation, installation height, nearby objects, and construction details affect resonance and impedance. Cut elements slightly long and make final adjustments with an antenna analyzer. Coax-loss results use representative cable data for planning; confirm the exact manufacturer's specifications and allow for connector, adapter, weather, age, moisture, and VSWR losses. Use Elmer Voice Browser requirements: Use a current browser, an HTTPS RigPi address, and allow microphone access for the RigPi site. Elmer voice input uses hosted speech recognition and works in supported desktop and mobile browsers, including current Chrome and Safari. Typed Ask Elmer questions and Elmer Control commands remain available when voice is unavailable. Chrome local-LAN microphone override: HTTPS remains the preferred method. If Chrome blocks microphone access to a trusted local RigPi address, open chrome://flags/#unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure . Enable Insecure origins treated as secure , enter the complete origin—normally http://rigpi5.local —and relaunch Chrome. Include the port when one is present. Reopen RigPi and grant microphone permission. Use this exception only for a trusted RigPi on the local network; it does not encrypt HTTP traffic and is not a substitute for HTTPS remote access. 1. Open Ask Elmer or the Elmer Control drawer and tap Elmer PTT . 2. Allow microphone access when the browser asks. The permission belongs to the RigPi site and browser being used. 3. After the tone, speak normally, then tap Elmer PTT again to finish. The button is push-to-talk; no wake phrase is needed. 4. Review any frequency or other safety-sensitive value that RigPi asks you to confirm. In Elmer Control, tap Affirm or Cancel , press Enter for the default Affirm action, or use Elmer PTT to speak the response. 5. Use the speaker control to enable or disable spoken playback. When enabled, Elmer reads answers, proposed actions, and results in an AI-generated voice. Elmer automatically recognizes supported languages, searches using English source material, and answers in the speaker's language. Elmer Control also accepts approval words in the language used for the command. Live captions can transcribe received audio and translate it to a selected language. Voice audio is sent to the hosted Elmer service only between the two Elmer PTT taps or while live captions are active. The listening indicator and tone show when capture begins. Turn off live captions when they are not needed. Use Elmer Control Open the Elmer Control drawer from the side tab in the main Tuner or Keyer window. Type a command and select Run , or tap Elmer PTT , speak after the tone, and tap it again when finished. Typed and spoken commands use the same control path; no wake phrase is required. When a command requires approval, Elmer displays the proposed action before changing the station. With spoken results enabled, Elmer reads the proposal first and the approval timer starts after the reading finishes. Respond with Affirm or Cancel , press Enter to choose the default Affirm button, or tap Elmer PTT and speak the response. Elmer then carries out the approved action and verifies the result when possible. Examples include: • Connect radio and power on • Disconnect radio • Tune to FT8 on 20 meters • Tune radio 1 to 14.025 MHz CW • Set mode to CW and bandwidth to 500 Hz • Split up 5 kHz • Split down 2 kHz • Split off • Restore the previous frequency and mode • Swap VFOs • Copy VFO A to VFO B • Set volume to 20 percent • Set microphone level to 50 percent • Set RF gain to 40 percent • Set CW speed to 22 words per minute • Put CQ CQ DE W6HN in the CW buffer • Run macro CW BW 500 HZ from bank 2 • Scan shortwave broadcasts in Spanish and stop on a signal Use the up/down triangles or keyboard Up/Down arrows to recall previous commands. During a supported scan, Space stops on the current frequency; press Space again to resume. Operator remains in control. Elmer uses allowlisted station actions, confirms sensitive changes, verifies results when possible, and does not treat ordinary text as permission to transmit. Check the selected radio, frequency, mode, bandwidth, power, antenna, and operating privileges before transmitting. Radio and browser troubleshooting Symptom What to check Elmer reports that radio control is unavailable. Open the Tuner and connect the selected radio first. Confirm that normal RigPi tuning works, then repeat the command. The microphone is unavailable. Use HTTPS, check the browser's microphone permission for the RigPi site, reload the page, and select the microphone again. For trusted local HTTP access in Chrome, use the documented Insecure origins treated as secure override. The wrong language is recognized. Check the voice-language selection. Automatic recognition usually works best when the command contains a complete phrase and a clearly spoken frequency. A spoken frequency is uncertain. Elmer should request confirmation. Cancel the change if the displayed frequency is not exactly what you intended, then type the command. The allowance is exhausted. Open View Usage . During the beta, contact the RigPi Elmer administrator; production plans and refills are managed through RigPi.net. References open the wrong page. Reload Ask Elmer and try the reference again. Official Help references resolve locally on the RigPi. Privacy and account scope • The station credential is stored on the RigPi and is never displayed in the browser. • QRZ and HamQTH passwords remain on the RigPi. Only facts requested for an answer are sent to the hosted Elmer service. • Station statistics contain operational totals; the station statistics page does not display question, answer, or feedback-comment text. • Answer feedback is optional. The feedback notice explains what is submitted before it is sent. After a Factory Reset The Elmer station credential is not restored from the RigPi user database backup. Sign in as administrator and pair RigPi Elmer Service again. Reconnect other external services whose protected credentials were not restored. RigPi Help — Set Up Ask Elmer, Elmer Voice and Elmer Control

pages.title: RigPi Introduction > Security
pages.text: ﻿ RigPi Introduction > Security Security << Click to Display Table of Contents >> Navigation: RigPi Introduction > Security Security RigPi controls station equipment and can transmit when an account has permission. Treat it like any other Internet-connected station controller: use strong account passwords, expose only the connection you need, install operating-system updates, and remove access that is no longer required. Never expose an unencrypted RigPi address to the Internet. Remote browsers should connect through a configured https:// DuckDNS or Cloudflare address (described below). Do not forward the RigPi web, SDR, SSH, database, VNC, or other service ports directly unless you understand and accept the risk. Local and remote connections A local address such as http://rigpi5.local can be used on a trusted home or station network. Secure remote operation requires HTTPS. In addition to encrypting browser traffic, HTTPS provides the secure browser context required for remote microphone access and other browser features. RigPi provides two HTTPS choices. Configure them under SETTINGS > Accounts > User Settings . Complete setup instructions are in External Accounts . Method Advantages Important limitations Native HTTPS with DuckDNS (free) Free permanent hostname; automatically renewed Let’s Encrypt certificate; direct connection to the station. Requires a reachable public IP address and router forwarding of TCP port 443. DuckDNS publishes the station’s public IP address. It generally does not work through carrier-grade NAT (CGNAT), double NAT, or blocked inbound ports without additional network changes. Cloudflare Tunnel (free plus your own domain) No router port forwarding; works through CGNAT and most restricted Internet connections; does not publish the station’s origin IP address. Uses a third-party tunnel service. A permanent named station address requires a domain owned by the station operator. Use the complete secure address. A remote address begins with https:// , not http:// . Test it from outside the station network, such as a phone with Wi-Fi disabled. Some routers cannot use the public address from inside the same LAN. Native HTTPS with DuckDNS RigPi obtains and renews the certificate and keeps the DuckDNS address synchronized with the station’s public IP address. Forward only external TCP port 443 to port 443 at the RigPi’s reserved local IP address. Do not forward port 80 or the individual SDR ports. Secure same-origin paths such as https://your-name.duckdns.org provide remote SDR access through the main RigPi HTTPS connection. There is no need to expose ports except for port 443. • Before enabling the forwarding rule, replace all factory or weak RigPi passwords. • Disable or move the router’s Internet administration page if it uses external port 443. • If the DuckDNS name resolves but the connection times out, compare the router’s WAN address with the public address shown by DuckDNS. A mismatch can indicate stale DNS, double NAT, or CGNAT. • The DuckDNS token is stored locally in a root-only file and is not returned to the browser. DuckDNS is naming and certificate support, not a privacy proxy. Anyone resolving the hostname can see the station’s public IP address. Choose Cloudflare Tunnel to conceal the origin address or to avoid inbound port forwarding. Cloudflare Tunnel Cloudflare Tunnel makes an outbound connection from RigPi to Cloudflare, so the router does not accept a new inbound connection and no port-forwarding rule is required. This is normally the better choice for CGNAT, double NAT, ISP-blocked inbound ports, or origin-IP concealment. Protect the Cloudflare account with a strong unique password and multi-factor authentication. Treat the tunnel token as a password: do not paste it into messages, screenshots, or support requests. Remove unused tunnels and DNS records from the Cloudflare dashboard. Accounts and station permissions • Give every guest user a separate RigPi account and a strong, unique password. • Reserve administrator access for people who must change system-wide settings. • Grant radio control and transmit permission only when required. Use a receive-only or restricted access level for observers. • Delete unused accounts promptly and review account requests before approval. • Do not share browser sessions. Sign out when using a shared or public computer. Browser audio, SDR, and site permissions Microphone permission is stored separately for each browser, device, and RigPi address. Permission granted to a local address does not automatically apply to its DuckDNS or Cloudflare address. Grant camera, microphone, clipboard, and notification permission only to the expected RigPi hostname. Temporary Remote Support Temporary Remote Support provides time-limited, key-only diagnostic access for a trusted technician. It can use a temporary encrypted address that requires no domain or router change, or an existing secure station address. • Verify the technician’s complete Ed25519 public key and fingerprint through a trusted channel. • Choose the shortest practical access period and remain available during the session. • Send only the displayed Support URL. Never send a private key, password, DuckDNS token, Cloudflare token, or API credential. • Select Revoke Now when the session is complete. Access also expires automatically and is cleared by a restart. Support access is powerful. An authorized technician can inspect and change the operating system. Enable it only for someone you trust. Firewall, intrusion protection, and updates RigPi includes the UFW firewall and Fail2ban as defense-in-depth measures. A firewall reduces unnecessary network exposure, and Fail2ban can temporarily block repeated failed login attempts. Neither replaces HTTPS, strong passwords, safe router configuration, or timely updates. See the UFW topic before changing firewall rules. Install Raspberry Pi OS and RigPi security updates promptly. Review unexpected login notifications and access logs. Avoid installing unneeded Internet-facing software, and remove services that are no longer used. Passwords, tokens, and backups • Use a password manager and never reuse the administrator password on another service. • Treat DuckDNS, Cloudflare, Elmer, SMTP, callbook, notification, VPN, and API credentials as sensitive. • Keep downloaded RigPi backups private. They can contain station records and account settings. • Do not include passwords, tokens, private keys, or personal information in screenshots or support messages. Factory Reset rebuilds the station database and removes managed DuckDNS, Cloudflare, Elmer, Remote Support, WireGuard, ZeroTier, browser, and other private station data. It also removes release-development backups managed by RigPi. Factory Reset does not delete the external DuckDNS hostname, Cloudflare tunnel, or DNS records from those providers’ accounts, and it intentionally preserves unrelated personal SSH keys. Remove those external records and keys separately before transferring a system. Remote-access checklist 1. Set strong, unique passwords and confirm each user’s permissions. 2. Choose one HTTPS method: DuckDNS for a direct connection with reachable port 443, or Cloudflare Tunnel when port forwarding or public-IP exposure is undesirable. 3. Use the secure same-origin SDR path, normally /sdr1 for the first account. The sdr1 option is entered in SETTINGS > Accounts > Account Editor. 4. Test from outside the station LAN and confirm the browser shows the expected HTTPS hostname. 5. Verify receive audio, microphone permission, radio control, and PTT into a dummy load. 6. Review accounts, tunnel settings, router rules, updates, and logs periodically.

pages.title: RigPi Introduction > Quick Start Guide
pages.text: ﻿ RigPi Introduction > Quick Start Guide RigPi-SDR Quick Start Guide << Click to Display Table of Contents >> Navigation: RigPi Introduction > RigPi-SDR Quick Start Guide What is Needed 1. RigPi Station Server (RSS) a. Raspberry Pi 4B+ or Raspberry Pi 5 (recommended) b . 5.1-volt, 3-amp Power Supply with a USB-C connector. c. An Ethernet cable or Wi-Fi Internet connection to your router d. Another computer or mobile device on the same network, or e. M onitor with a micro HDMI connector. USB keyboard and USB mouse f. For remote operations, a browser on your mobile device 2. Ham Radio Transceiver a. CAT USB interface cable (or serial-to-USB adapter) for control and (if supported) audio b. Audio cables for VoIP or digital mode software (or a radio with internal audio CODECs), CW and PTT cables, or via CAT. Connecting RSS to the Internet (Ethernet Connection) The drawings below are for the original MFJ-1234 which uses a Raspberry Pi3B+ board. The MFJ-1234B/C have a slightly different design to accommodate the connectors on a Raspberry Pi 4B. 1. Connect an Ethernet cable from your router to RigPi Station Server. 2. Plug in the RSS 5.1-volt power supply. The two lights below the RSS KEY jack indicate power (red) and activity (green). The green light blinks as RigPi boots. The red light should not blink except once during booting. If it does, your power supply may be underrated or faulty. 3. On another computer or mobile device connected to the same network, open a browser window. Navigate to rigpi5.local. Apple Bonjour is required on Windows computers to find rigpi5.local. See the Technical topic in Help for more information on Bonjour. Without Bonjour, you can use the RigPi IP address instead. Log in to your router and look at connected devices. You will see the Raspberry Pi listed there along with its IP address. 4. The RSS Login screen appears after RSS has completed the boot process. (See below.) Connecting RSS to the Internet (Wi-Fi Connection) RSS has built-in Wi-Fi if an Ethernet connection isn't convenient. If you need to connect using Wi-Fi rather than using an Ethernet connection, a monitor/keyboard/mouse must be connected to RSS to set it up. 1. Connect a computer monitor having a micro HDMI input, USB keyboard and USB mouse to RSS. 2. Plug in the RSS 5.1-volt power supply. The two lights below the RSS KEY jack indicate power (red) and activity (green). The green light blinks as RigPi boots. The red light should not blink except once during boot. If it does, the power supply may be underrated or faulty. 3. The Raspbian Wayland Desktop appears after RSS has completed the boot process. 4. In the upper-right corner of the Desktop click the Network icon (Up/Down arrow). 5. Select Turn on Wi-Fi, then click the Network button again. 6. Select the network you wish to join from the list. 7. In the Pre Shared Key box enter your Wi-Fi password, then click OK. 8. While the Desktop is open, click the Raspberry Menu icon and navigate to Preferences>Control Centre>Localization. 9. Enter the Locale, Timezone, Keyboard and Wi-Fi Country for your location. 10. Click the RSS icon (a Pi symbol) to start RSS. The RSS Login screen appears. Set Screen Resolution (for VNC connection to desktop) To change the VNC desktop to a higher or lower resolution, a Screen Configuration program is provided with Trixie. Open the Application menu on the desktop and go to Preferences>Control Centre->Screens. Select the resolution you wish to use. Go to Configure->Apply to set the resolution. Set Screen Resolution (for HDMI connection to desktop) To set the HDMI resolution on a Raspberry Pi running the Trixie distribution, follow these steps: 1. Open the terminal on your Raspberry Pi or connect to it remotely using SSH. 2. Edit the configuration file for the HDMI settings using the following command: sudo nano /boot//firmware/config.txt 3. Look for the lines related to HDMI settings. Scroll down or use the arrow keys to navigate. You should see lines starting with `hdmi_group` and `hdmi_mode`. 4. Uncomment the desired `hdmi_group` and `hdmi_mode` lines by removing the '#' character at the beginning of each line. Refer to the official Raspberry Pi documentation for the available HDMI modes and their corresponding values. 5. Once you have uncommented the desired lines, save the changes by pressing Ctrl + X, then Y, and finally Enter to confirm. 6. Reboot the Raspberry Pi for the changes to take effect. You can reboot by running the following command: sudo reboot After the reboot, the HDMI resolution should be set according to the values you specified in the `config.txt` file. Connecting your Radio RigPi controls the frequency and mode of your radio through a CAT (Computer Aided Tuning) connection to a USB port. Most modern radios provide a USB connection which require a USB A-B cable. Older radios have a variety of connection requirements, although each manufacturer is usually consistent from one radio to another. Check the manual for your radio for specifics on what type of cable is required. Manufacturer Older Model CAT Connection Kenwood DB9 Serial, requires serial-to-USB adapter Icom CI-V 3.5mm, requires CI-V-to-USB adapter Yaesu DB9 Serial, requires serial-to-USB adapter. Older Yaesu radios also require a level converter. Audio connections to your radio are covered later in this manual. CW Keying requires either a cable between the KEY jack on RSS and your radio's keying input (more later), or CAT control. Accessing RigPi RigPi 5 is accessed by entering rigpi5.local in a browser's navigation bar. If your browser can't find rigpi5.local, it may be necessary to install Bonjour on your computer. See Bonjour Help elsewhere in this manual for details. Alternatively you can use the IP address of RigPi 5 as found in the list of connected devices in your router. Exploring RSS, Startup Windows The RigPi Login screen is shown below. If you have set up a schedule for rig use, additional information will be shown on the Login window. 1. RSS initially uses Username 'admin' and no (blank) Password. 2. Enter admin in the USERNAME box. 3. If you are a guest and want your callsign to be recognized, enter it in the CALLSIGN box. Passwords are required for Guest accounts. 4. A guest can request an account by clicking the Request an Account button. 5. For the Admin account, p ress Enter (leaving the Password field blank). 6. The RigPi Express User Settings window appears next. RSS Express Settings have two windows designed to get you going rapidly. Express User Settings has fields for your Call, location, and optional QRZ XML subscription credentials. You must enter your call before proceeding. Click Fill Below from Callbook to enter your name, state and grid square. If you haven't specified QRZ credentials, RigPi uses the onboard FCC database to fill in the information. The FCC option only works for US calls. Click NEXT to go to the Express Radio Settings window. Express Radio Settings is configured with the Hamlib simulated radio, Dummy. You can set up your own radio or continue to use Dummy by skipping the Express Radio Settings. Note: RigPi uses the default Baud rate for your radio in the Express Radio Settings window. If you have changed the radio's Baud rate you must use that Baud rate in RigPi. Skip the Express Radio Settings window and enter the Baud rate in SETTINGS->Advanced Radio. When done, click NEXT. Back Up Your Memory Card Memory cards have a limited lifetime, so it is good practice to back up your card as insurance. For details on how to make a backup copy please refer to the System topic in the Troubleshooting section of Help. Shutting Down Never disconnect the RigPi Station Server power supply without shutting down the RigPi Raspberry Pi first. Disrupting the power before shutting down can corrupt the microSD memory card. To shut down RigPi: 1. Go to SETTINGS>System. 2. Click the Shutdown button. 3. Wait for the green activity light on the Raspberry Pi to stop blinking. 4. Disconnect the power. Enjoy RigPi! Additional Help is available • RSS Toolbar HELP • ASK ELMER on the RigPi toolbar or in the Help menu • Online forum: RigPi Forum • RigPi online help: Online Help • PDF Help file: Help PDF

pages.title: Views > SDR 4
pages.text: ﻿ Views > SDR 4 SDR 4 << Click to Display Table of Contents >> Navigation: Views > SDR 4 SDR4 is the administrator's SDR dashboard. It displays up to four account SDR workspaces together, so you can view multiple configured receivers from one page. Open the dashboard 1. Sign in with an administrator account. 2. Select SDR4 in the RigPi navigation bar. 3. Identify each workspace by the account callsign or username shown above it. 4. Use the controls inside a workspace to connect and operate its configured SDR. Which accounts appear? The dashboard uses the first four active accounts in user-ID order. Each workspace is opened with that account's SDR path and radio number. Empty positions display No SDR . SDR4 presents the configured workspaces; it does not create additional hardware receivers. Simultaneous operation depends on the receivers and services available to those accounts. Audio and a larger view Start audio in the workspace you want to hear. If several workspaces play audio, their sound can overlap; stop audio in the others when listening to one receiver. For a larger single-account workspace, open Elmer . See RigPi-SDR for tuning, spectrum, waterfall, audio and display controls.

pages.title: Settings > Scheduler
pages.text: ﻿ Settings > Scheduler Scheduler << Click to Display Table of Contents >> Navigation: Settings > Scheduler RigPi Scheduler is the settings window for RigPi Calendar. Scheduler provides a way to add events to Calendar for any day of the year. Events include reservations for rig use and custom events such as club meetings or skeds. You can overlay the Scheduler with event lists from external sources, such as contests. < Go to previous month (or week/day/list delending on selected clanedar format). > Go to next month (or week/day/list depending on selected calendar format). today Show current month, week, day or list for current day. month/week/day/list Select calendar range. Users A list of users, including radio name, call, and username. Drag a user bar to the desired date to schedule. Add Add custom events. Yellow day Current day. The "hamburger" button in the upper right corner of the Scheduler has additional options: Add a calendar overlay for ham contests and holidays. Remove all events. Remove custom events. Selecting Digital Contests adds the digital contest overlay to the calendar. Each digital contest use a lavender color. A bar indicates an event lasting all day, while an event occurring at a specific time in the date has a colored dot. custom.ics Swedish calendar iCalShare.com cw.ics Ham CW contests DL2NBY digital.ics Ham digital contests DL2NBY phone.ics Ham phone contests DL2NBY Events_in_History.ics Events in US history americanhistorycalendar.com JapanHolidays.ics Japanese holidays SwedishHolidays.ics Swedish Holidays (duplicate of custom) iCalShare.com UKHolidays.ics UK Holidays iCalShare.com us_hol.ics US Holidays https://www.thunderbird.net/en-US/calendar/holidays Reserving a time slot Each user account can be given reservations with start and end times. The RigPi Log In window shows current and upcoming reservations. To set a specific time slot during the day for an event, open the day view and navigate to the day you want to edit. Drag the bar from the top to the starting time, then drag the bottom of the bar to the ending time.

pages.title: Technical > Schematics
pages.text: ﻿ Technical > Schematics Schematics << Click to Display Table of Contents >> Navigation: Technical > Schematics Schematics and additional information for the K1EL Winkeyer 2 are here . Schematics for the MFJ RigPi Audio and RigPi Keyer boards can be downloaded through the following link: MFJ RigPi Schematics RigPi Audio Circuit Description The MFJ RigPi Audio board is based on the Cirrus Logic WM8731 (U1) low power stereo Codec. It supports a stereo input and mono output. The left input and output channels are transformer isolated for hum reduction. Both stereo input channels are available for I/Q signal processing. This input path is not transformer isolated. The WM8731 is controlled through the Raspberry Pi GPIO connector. GPIO 1 (Pin 12) BCLK: Digital Au00io Bit Clock, Pull Down, GPIO 19 (Pin 35) LRC: DAC Sample Rate Left/Right Clock GPIO 20 (Pin 38) ADCDAT: Digital data out GPIO 21 (Pin 40) DACDAT: Digital data in SDA (Pin 3) SDIN: 3-Wire MPU Data Input / 2-Wire MPU Data Input SCL (pin 5) SCLK: 3-Wire MPU Clock Input / 2-Wire MPU Clock Input The WM8731 can convert input data with up to a 96kb sample rate. Additional GPIO pins used for RigPi Audio: GPIO 17 (Pin 11): PTT Connectors: J1: Raspberry Pi GPIO connector J2: 3.5 mm jack for I/Q input (stereo, unisolated) J3: 3.5 mm jack for left channel audio input (tip, transformer isolated) J4: 3.5 mm jack for audio (tip), PTT (ring), and KX3 (ring) power on signal J5: Connector to route audio to the RigPi jumper board Jumpers: JP2: Audio In selection (1-2 for stereo -no transformer isolation-, 2-3 for left mono -transformer isolatedinput) RigPi Keyer Circuit Description The K1EL WinKeyer3 CW Keyer IC provides all of the programming for its many features. The keyer is controlled through the internal serial port on the Raspberry Pi, ttyS0. RXD (Pin 8): Receive data (from keyer) TXD (Pin 10): Transmit data (to keyer) Connectors: J201: Raspberry Pi GPIO connector J202: 3.5 mm jack, PTT out (tip is PTT, ring is 5V pull-up) J203: 3.5 mm jack, Paddle input (tip is DOT, ring is DASH) J204: 3.5 mm keying output (tip keys, ring not used) J205: speaker connection J206: PB-NET (allows external switches to play back internal memory, not used) J207: Programming connector, not used Jumpers: JP201: PTT enable (1-2 enables GPIO PTT, otherwise, GPIO PTT not used) GPIO pins used for RigPi Keyer: GPIO 9 (Pin 21): Data to radio keyer (only used at remote end) GPIO 10 (Pin 19): Data from remote keyer (only used at radio end) GPIO 17 (Pin 11): PTT RXD (Pin 8): Receive data from keyer chip TXD: (Pin 10): Transmit data to keyer chip

pages.title: Other Programs > Update RSS Files
pages.text: ﻿ Other Programs > Update RSS Files Update RSS Files << Click to Display Table of Contents >> Navigation: Other Programs > Update RSS Files Updating the files for RSS is done automatically when a new minor version is detected, or manually from the SETTINGS>System menu. Updates provided on the https://rigpi.net server are downloaded to RSS, unzipped and copied to the correct RSS folders. Only files newer than a corresponding file are updated. The update retains all user settings and databases. To update manually: 1. In RSS go to SETTINGS>System and click Update RSS Files. If a new version is detected, click OK to proceed. 2. When the update is done click OK to reboot RigPi to refresh all files. Updating RSS files does not update any system files or other installed programs.
